summary: Master network planning with traffic matrix calculation, MPLS engineering, and failure simulation. 5-day advanced course for Network Architects.
lede: Network planning and optimization helps network architects and operations leads model demand and plan capacity against performance and SLA targets. They build traffic matrices from NetFlow and interface measurements, optimize routing with OSPF, BGP and MPLS techniques, and simulate failures to assess resilience and SLA performance.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for senior professionals responsible for designing, maintaining, and optimizing high-performance networks that support critical business operations.
audience: Senior Network Operations Manager - Oversee daily
Data Center Network Engineer - Design scalable
Wireless LAN Architect - Plan and optimize
Network Security Analyst - Integrate security policies
Cloud Infrastructure Engineer - Align network capacity
IT Infrastructure Director - Set strategic network
modules: Foundations of Network Planning and Demand Modeling
Traffic Matrix Calculation and Demand Estimation
IP Routing Design and Topology Optimization
MPLS Traffic Engineering and Load Balancing
Network Simulation and Failure Scenario Validation
Wireless LAN Planning and Virtualization Considerations
Advanced Traffic Engineering and Optimization Strategies
Executive Reporting and Strategic Roadmap Synthesis
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Advanced working knowledge of IP routing (OSPF, BGP), Layer 2/3 switching, and subnetting. Participants must understand fundamental traffic engineering concepts and have experience with network monitoring tools (e.g., NetFlow, SNMP). No coding required, but familiarity with Excel for data analysis is essential. This course is designed for intermediate-to-advanced professionals; beginners should complete a foundational networking course first.
